Tuned BMW M4 Goes Official With Unicorn Puke Livery
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozport
Is there anything that hasn’t been said about the second-generation BMW M4 ? Probably not. After all, this model blew six candles off its birthday cake this year, so it’s not exactly new anymore.
Moreover, it also underwent its first (and probably only) mid-cycle refresh, with the LCI, which means Life Cycle Impulse and is Bimmer slang for facelift, going official at the beginning of 2024. The LCI brought new lights, fresh wheels, some tweaks on the inside, and more power reserved for the top-of-the-line version, and is meant to keep this model on the competitive side of the class until its successor arrives, probably toward the end of the decade.
Word on the street is that the third-generation BMW M4 might arrive after 2029, because the current one’s production has been extended until that year. Chances are it will debut as a normal 4 Series first, with the full-blown M model joining the lineup eventually, and one does not need to be a BMW connoisseur to find out what it will look like, because all they have to do is look at the all-new 3 Series, which is a Neue Klasse model both inside and out, and rides on the an updated version of the old car’s CLAR platform.
The 4er is a slightly sportier take on the 3er, replacing the two-door body styles (coupe and convertible) versions of the F3X 3 Series, and also launching a liftback that is known as the Gran Coupe. The M4 Coupe and M4 Convertible are two-door versions of the M3, and the same will apply to the next generation.
Photo: Instagram | revozport But we are venturing a bit too far from the story here, so we will get back on track by stating the obvious: the M4 may not be new anymore, but it can still make headlines. And it is usually a tuned example that ends up in our news feed, or one that is searching for a new home on the used car market. This is a case of the former, and the tuner’s name behind the project is RevoZport .
The quoted company recently introduced some tuning kits for the F95 X5 M, the demised M8 Coupe, and the outgoing X6 M, and they were quite interesting, for the most part. And for what it’s worth, so is this BMW M4 Coupe, which features some of its visual extras on the outside. But the add-ons, which have likely been made of carbon fiber, are not the things that help it stand out, because that would be the livery.
As mentioned in the title, it definitely looks like unicorn puke, and it mixes what seem to be the typical BMW M colors on a white background, and with a very trippy pattern. The large front splitter, the side skirt extensions, the special trim on the front fenders, the rear diffuser, ducktail spoiler, and massive wing that sits on the trunk lid have all come from the quoted tuner’s portfolio.
And these are not the only things, because this BMW M4 Coupe is also wider than the standard one, though you may not be able to tell at first, and that is due to the trippy livery. The wheels do not look that special, and by that we mean that they do not seem to have come from the aftermarket world. But we could be wrong. After all, it’s not like we are wheel experts, and if we are indeed wrong, then please accept our apologies in advance.
Photo: Instagram | revozport RevoZport did not have much to say about this modified BMW M4 Coupe other than the fact that it features parts from its “Aero Kit,” and that it is “track ready.” There’s no doubt that this things will turn heads wherever it goes. After all, it’s not like it is a kitschy build, despite the livery, but what is your take on that?
Actually, before inviting you to answer in the comments section at the bottom of the page, we also have to mention the car’s oily bits, reminding you that all versions of the modern-day M4 (and not only) pack a 3.0-liter inline-six engine, with twin turbocharging.
The base BMW M4 Coupe has 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW) on tap. The mid-range M4 Competition Coupe is offered with 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW), and the top-of-the-line M4 Competition xDrive Coupe has 523 hp (530 ps/390 kW) available via the right pedal. The 0 to 60 mph (0-97 kph) acceleration is deployed in 4.1, 3.8, and 3.4 seconds, respectively, and for what it’s worth, the latter model is actually faster than the iconic Ferrari Enzo.
Pricing starts at $82,200 for the M4 Coupe, $86,400 for the M4 Competition, and $91,500 for the M4 Competition xDrive, and the M4 Competition xDrive Convertible has an MSRP of $98,400 attached to it in the United States of America.
